transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Orion), Tom Brewer (Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (CTO)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm with Ravi our SE. quick intro then we'll, uh, kick off with your goals for the call
00:22 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Thanks Maya, yeah I'm Aisha, CTO at Orion, joining with Lena and Tom. We're evaluating Redwood for some LLM infra, main things: fast POC via PLG, but also thinking about Dedicated / Private for later
00:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, that's exactly what we do. quick question — what's your current stack? are you using OpenAI or self-hosted models today?
00:51 Speaker 3 (Lena): We're mixed — experimenting with OpenAI for prototypes, and we have some internal HF models served on Vertex-ish infra, but it's a mess. latency's hit or miss, cost is creeping up
01:10 Speaker 2 (Tom): Platform side we run EKS, and we have strict VPC rules. If we go private we need SSO + audit logs + KMS. Also curious about time to first token — we need devs to be able to hit an endpoint within an hour, ideally minutes
01:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): Totally, the Redwood Quickstart is designed for that — self-serve sign-up, free credits, SDKs — you can get a token and do a cURL in under 10 minutes in most cases. we'll send the quickstart link after.
01:54 Speaker 4 (Ravi): And from an SE perspective, we have sample repo and SDKs, plus a one-click demo app. For latency: hosted API is fastest to get going; dedicated gives more predictable throughput; private gives the strongest controls for compliance
02:18 Speaker 3 (Lena): How do you handle KV cache and batching? For our chat use case we really care about cost per token with long contexts
02:31 Speaker 4 (Ravi): We do automatic prefix caching and workload-aware batching. There's also config you can tweak — e.g., enable prefix cache for chat to reduce repeated compute. Our Optimize toolkit analyzes token patterns and suggests quantization / batching settings
02:55 Speaker 3 (Lena): Nice. And what's the free credits policy? Is there a frictionless way for devs to sign up?
03:04 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, self-serve with email, you get an initial credit pool for eval. If you want a larger trial tied to a POC, we can provision dedicated eval credits — we'll coordinate that with you.
03:18 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Security is key. Do you have SOC2? And SSO/SAML for console access? Also we need customer-managed KMS for Private deployments
03:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): We're SOC2 Type II. SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported for the console. For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide audit logs. I'll share our security pack in the follow-up
03:46 Speaker 4 (Ravi): small note: sometimes the transcribed product names get munged in exports, but yes, Private supports KMS and we can do air-gapped installs for regulated customers
04:02 Speaker 3 (Lena): What's the typical timeline if we start with hosted and then move to Dedicated? How disruptive is model pinning/rollouts?
04:12 Speaker 4 (Ravi): We support model pinning and rollout policies at the route level. Moving from hosted to dedicated is mostly a config/route change — your app calls the same API surface. We help with migration and run a canary rollout to minimize impact
04:33 Speaker 2 (Tom): Any limits on model catalog? We use a mix of open models and internal fine-tuned ones
04:42 Speaker 4 (Ravi): You can bring your own model for Dedicated/Private, and we host a curated catalog for hosted mode. For internal models you'd typically use Private or Dedicated depending on tenancy needs
05:00 Speaker 3 (Lena): Can we run a benchmark? We want to measure p95 latency for our 2k token prompts and cost per 1M tokens
05:11 Speaker 1 (Maya): Absolutely. Ravi will share a benchmark checklist and a sample set of prompts. We can run a small benchmark on hosted or on a dedicated eval pool — whichever you prefer
05:26 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Also, note that quantized model variants can drastically lower cost, we'll recommend a profile once we see your workload
05:36 Speaker 2 (Aisha): For compliance, do you store customer data? What about retention and deletion controls?
05:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hosted defaults to not retain customer payloads for production customers; we have options for retention policies and detailed audit logs. For Private, data never leaves customer's network. We'll include the retention matrix in the security docs
06:02 Speaker 3 (Lena): Good. For onboarding, is there a sample app for Slack-ish assistant and embeddings pipeline?
06:12 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Yep — sample apps for chat, embeddings, vector store integrations. Also we provide an eval harness to measure quality regressions tied to prompt sets
06:24 Speaker 2 (Tom): Network requirements — outbound ports, IP allowlist, anything special for hosted?
06:31 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Hosted is standard HTTPS outbound; we also support IP allowlisting and dedicated egress for Dedicated. For Private you'll need VPC peering or private link — we'll work with your infra team
06:46 Speaker 3 (Lena): One pain we had with other vendors was long onboarding — lots of seams between docs and SDKs. How's your SDK maturity? Languages?
06:56 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have official SDKs for Python, JS, and Go. Docs are example-driven. The PLG quickstart focuses on minimal friction: get API key, run a sample, see results. We'll share step-by-step that gets you to first token in ~5-10 min
07:14 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Pricing — want a sense of hosted per-token and Dedicated commit model. Also, what about burst capacity?
07:24 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Hosted is usage-based per token. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; you can enable burst capacity for short spikes. Maya will include a pricing sheet in follow-up
07:35 Speaker 3 (Lena): For POC success criteria: p95 latency under 700ms for 1k prompts, integration with our SSO, and cost under $X per 1M tokens — we'll flesh out numbers in the pilot doc
07:51 Speaker 1 (Maya): Perfect. Let's capture that as part of next steps. We'll also set up a sandbox project for you with free credits so devs can self-serve
08:03 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Quick technical Q — our models use long KV caches and token window of 8k. Any gotchas on serving long contexts?
08:14 Speaker 4 (Ravi): (cont) Our runtime supports long context and KV cache management; we tune kernels and batching for long-sequence workloads. For really long contexts we may recommend model sharding or retrieval augmentation to keep costs down
08:32 Speaker 3 (Lena): Are there per-route SLOs and tracing hooks we can use to debug latency regressions?
08:39 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Yes, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, token-level cost breakdowns in the Console. You can also instrument tracing on client side to correlate request lifecycle
08:50 Speaker 2 (Tom): Anything special about keys and rotation? We need secure key rotation for prod
08:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): API keys support rotation, and Private can integrate with your KMS for keys. We'll include key rotation docs in the security pack
09:07 Speaker 3 (Lena): Ok good. If we sign up for trial today, how long until our devs can start testing?
09:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Usually under 10 minutes to first token for hosted accounts. For Dedicated eval pools it's a bit longer — a day or two to provision if you need reserved capacity for benchmarking, but we can usually spin up a small eval cluster quickly
09:29 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Any known limitations around EU data residency? We're partially EU-based
09:36 Speaker 4 (Ravi): We have region options; for Hosted we can route to EU regions and we support Private deployments in customer regions. We'll surface data residency options in the follow-up doc
09:48 Speaker 3 (Lena): Sounds good. On the integration side, Tom will need the network/team docs, and I'll need the benchmark checklist and sample prompts
09:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. I'll send pricing and quickstart. Ravi, can you share the benchmark checklist after the call?
10:04 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Yep, I'll drop that and include sample warmup prompts and a small script to run p95 measurements
10:13 Speaker 2 (Tom): One more question — for Private deployments, what's the typical lead time and support model?
10:20 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Private deployments vary: 4-8 weeks typical depending on network and compliance needs. We offer an enterprise onboarding package and dedicated SRE support for Private customers
10:34 Speaker 3 (Lena): Cool. Any reason not to start hosted quickstart while we evaluate Private feasibility?
10:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): No reason — that's the recommended path. Start hosted to iterate quickly, run bench, then if committed move to Dedicated or Private with minimal app changes
10:50 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Great. Let's talk scheduling — can we do pilot kickoff on Feb 3rd?
10:56 Speaker 1 (Maya): Feb 3rd works. I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
11:04 Speaker 3 (Lena): Thanks everyone.
11:07 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks all — recap: Maya send pricing + quickstart, Ravi send benchmark checklist, Orion team create trial account and confirm network/VPC constraints. Schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-02-03.
11:24 Speaker 2 (Tom): We'll get those items done, talk soon.

End of transcript
